target_photo: genuine tiny inner ligule separated from longer outside sheath-mouth hairs

discovery.curator: Pamela Borden Trewatha, Ph.D. — Missouri State University, Plant Identification
discovery.source_caption: Missouri State identifies a lower ligule view and an upper collar view of Eragrostis spectabilis.
discovery.visual_review: The 500-pixel source ligule image depicts a white hair-bearing opened blade/sheath region, but no physical ruler. It is better morphological orientation than extant outside-only photos. Fine 0.2–0.4 mm ligule length is NOT measured from it.

source_rights.rights_summary: Photographs belong to Dr. Trewatha unless otherwise noted. She says single-use educational and website reuse is without fee WITH explicit prior permission.
source_rights.must_not: Do not download/commit as public gallery photograph, display embedded website copy, or place leaf-organ arrows on these third-party files until written permission explicitly covers this website and overlays/adaptation.
source_rights.permission_request_scope: Ask permission for both specified photographs on the publicly viewable but genuinely noncommercial https://crking92.github.io/Hays-County-Botany/, visible creator/source credit and possible educational SVG arrow overlays; request higher-resolution originals if available, author credit, and any restrictions.

scientific_controls.reported_true_ligule: Burnet County: white truncate densely short-ciliate 0.2–0.4 mm
scientific_controls.reported_longer_sheath_hairs: Burnet County: outer tuft 2–4 mm, not a substitute for inner ligule
scientific_controls.need_local_capture: Confirm flowering E. spectabilis on same plant; pull/peel blade back from sheath, photograph interior straight-on with 1-mm scale, separate exterior 2–4 mm hairs, record rooted rhizome and whole flowering plant.

photo_search_status: Exact-source anatomical photos located but withheld due to permission; no scientifically confirmed freely licensed measured inner ligule photo installed.
